video_title: Can the Knicks go back-to-back? 👀 + Karl-Anthony Towns extension talks | NBA Today

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Brunson's recovery status ahead of Knicks training camp
quotes.excerpt: he's at about 80 to 85 percent after that wrist surgery that he had in July
quotes.quote: One thing you didn't see on Jalen Brunson's wrist was a brace because he's at about 80 to 85 percent after that wrist surgery that he had in July. He's back to doing basketball activity. He's had no restrictions when training camp begins in a couple of weeks as the Knicks begin their bid to repeat. It's almost amazing that he was able to produce that finals performance with his wrist ailing him that required surgery, but he should be and will be ready to go when training camp begins on September 29th.

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Status of Karl-Anthony Towns' contract extension talks with Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Both sides are in discussions. He's up for four years, 276 million dollars.
quotes.quote: Both sides are in discussions. He's up for four years, 276 million dollars. Also remember, James Dolan has said, I do not want this franchise to be in the second apron, so it's a lot to balance between both sides. Karl-Anthony Towns wants his extension. He wanted it last season, played through the season. It clearly did not bother them as they got to an NBA title, but also remember this: Josh Hart, up for an extension. Next year, Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby will be up for an extension. So it's something that the Knicks probably want to get done because you don't want to have so many balls in the air with guys as you're trying to repeat this season.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Knicks and Anthony Davis facing massive player option decisions
quotes.excerpt: their player options that they have for the following season are both enormous, over 60 million dollars.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Typically at this spot, you would definitely want to have a star player like Karl-Anthony Towns under contract. You'd never want to go into the last year of a deal. But I think he and Anthony Davis are in an interesting situation because their player options that they have for the following season are both enormous, over 60 million dollars. And the Knicks and the Wizards too aren't 100 percent sure that those two players are going to opt out of their contracts.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: In the case of Anthony Davis, they've tabled the talks. And so we'll see how long Karl-Anthony Towns is willing to discuss this. He will set the tone on this at media day. He's going to get asked about whether he's willing to talk about this into the season. If not, it'll create a deadline and we'll see whether the Knicks prioritize getting something done or not.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Concerns regarding the depth of the Knicks' frontcourt
quotes.excerpt: is this frontcourt too thin right now?
quotes.quote: The one question people have is, is there a championship hangover? And my one question is, is this frontcourt too thin right now? When you look at, certainly you've got Karl-Anthony Towns and you've got OG Anunoby, and you did sign Andre Drummond on a veteran minimum and you brought back Muhammad Diawara. Is this frontcourt thin? You have basically an open competition right now for that 14th roster spot between James Wiseman, the former top three pick in the draft, and Drew Eubanks right now. And remember, they also signed John Konchar. So one of those three are going to probably make the roster here. That's the biggest concern for me.

quotes.speaker: Vincent Goodwill
quotes.summary_phrase: Eastern Conference competition poses a challenge for Knicks' repeat bid
quotes.excerpt: The Philadelphia 76ers is loading up with Jaylen Brown and LeBron James.
quotes.quote: The biggest challenge to repeat sometimes is within. But when you look at the Eastern Conference and they've recognized this, the Philadelphia 76ers is loading up with Jaylen Brown and LeBron James. The Indiana Pacers, they have beaten the Knicks twice in the playoffs in the last three years. Tyrese Haliburton is back. Ivica Zubac is over there to replace Miles Turner. That's a team that's not afraid of the New York Knicks. The Miami Heat with Giannis Antetokounmpo. It is a reconfigured Eastern Conference. Because of the fact that nobody has repeated since the Stephen Curry, Kevin Durant Golden State Warriors, you know that the Knicks are going to be on high alert.
